title: Functorial Serre duality for line bundles on smooth projective schemes
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $Y$ be a smooth projective $F$-scheme of pure dimension $n\geq0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism]. Put $\omega_Y=\bigwedge^n\Omega^1_{Y/F}$, where the differential sheaf is obtained by gluing the affine Kähler differential modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the exterior power is the alternating quotient of the tensor power, with $\bigwedge^0=\mathcal O_Y$. For every invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $E$ [def-sc-invertible-module], put $E^\vee=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(E,\mathcal O_Y)$. There are $F$-linear isomorphisms
$$\theta_E^j:H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes E^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_F(H^{n-j}(Y,E),F)\qquad(j\geq0),$$
with $H^r(Y,E)=0$ for $r<0$. The groups on both sides are finite dimensional. Here $H^j$ is Zariski module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], and tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The isomorphisms are natural: for any morphism of invertible modules $v:E\to E'$, the map $H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes(E')^\vee)\to H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes E^\vee)$ induced by $\operatorname{id}_{\omega_Y}\otimes v^\vee$ corresponds to precomposition by $H^{n-j}(Y,v)$. In particular $H^j(Y,\omega_Y\otimes E^\vee)=0$ for $j>n$. Neither geometric integrality nor connectedness of $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0FVV (lemma-duality-proper-over-field), especially (5),(7); Tag 0FVX (remark-coherent-duality-proper-over-field) for naturality; Tag 0FW0 (remark-rework-duality-locally-free-CM) for the locally free pairing. This is the line-module consequence in the final sentence of Popa Theorem 1.6.6 proof.

proof.text: Write $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $f$ is proper. In particular it is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its only fibre is $Y$, of dimension at most $n$. Smoothness and pure dimension $n$ say that $f$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{Y/F}$ is locally free of rank $n$. On a common trivializing cover for this sheaf and $E$ [def-sc-invertible-module], the wedge of a basis identifies $\omega_Y$ with $\mathcal O_Y$ (the empty wedge is $1$ for $n=0$), and the dual basis identifies $E^\vee$ with $\mathcal O_Y$. Thus $G_E=\omega_Y\otimes E^\vee$ is locally free of rank one. On affine subopens these are associated free rank-one modules, so $G_E$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]. These local descriptions also identify the differential sheaf and exterior power used here with those in the trace-pairing node.

For $0\leq j\leq n$, set $i=n-j$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-proper-coherent-trace-pairing] to $Y/F$ and the rank-one locally free module $E$. It gives a single trace $t_Y:H^n(Y,\omega_Y)\to F$ and a perfect pairing $P_{E,i}$ between $H^i(Y,E)$ and $H^j(Y,E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y)$, both finite dimensional. The coefficient isomorphism $s_E:\omega_Y\otimes E^\vee\to E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y$, $w\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes w$, has inverse the same interchange, so its cohomology map is an isomorphism. Define $\theta_E^j(z)(x)=P_{E,i}(x,H^j(s_E)z)$. Bilinearity makes this $F$-linear. Perfection means precisely that the map from the second factor to the linear dual of the first is bijective; composition with $H^j(s_E)$ gives the required isomorphism. Its formula is cup product in the order $x,H^j(s_E)z$, followed by evaluation and $t_Y$.

For a map $v:E\to E'$, put $b=v^\vee\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\omega_Y}:(E')^\vee\otimes\omega_Y\to E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y$. Ordinary module cup product is natural for these coefficient maps: [lem-sc-scalar-cup-coefficient-naturality] gives naturality of scalar Ext cup, and [lem-sc-scalar-cup-module-cup-compatibility] identifies it with $(-1)^{ij}$ times the ordinary cup of [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product]. The same sign occurs in source and target, and its square is $1$, so cancellation gives ordinary cup naturality. Locally evaluation satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_E(e,b(\lambda'\otimes w))=\lambda'(v(e))w=\operatorname{ev}_{E'}(v(e),\lambda'\otimes w)$. This equality of sheaf maps and the two coefficient naturality squares therefore give $P_{E,i}(x,H^j(b)y)=P_{E',i}(H^i(v)x,y)$ after applying the same trace $t_Y$. Also $b\circ s_{E'}=s_E\circ(\operatorname{id}_{\omega_Y}\otimes v^\vee)$ on the elementary tensors $w\otimes\lambda'$. Substitute $y=H^j(s_{E'})z$ into the pairing equality. Step 2 then gives $\theta_E^j(H^j(\operatorname{id}\otimes v^\vee)z)(x)=\theta_{E'}^j(z)(H^i(v)x)$ for every $x$. Equality of linear functionals is pointwise equality, proving the asserted square, including noninvertible and zero maps $v$.

proof.text: If $j>n$, apply [lem-sfb-proper-quasicoherent-fibre-dimension-vanishing] to $f$ and $G_E$. Step 1 verified properness, the fibre dimension bound, and quasi-coherence, so $R^jf_*G_E=0$. The target $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is affine and $f$ is quasi-compact and separated, so [lem-pc-cohomology-sections-affine-base] gives $H^j(Y,G_E)\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}F,R^jf_*G_E)=0$. The stated negative-degree convention gives $H^{n-j}(Y,E)=0$, so its linear dual is zero as well. Define $\theta_E^j$ to be the unique map between these zero vector spaces; it is bijective and the naturality square commutes because all its maps have zero source and target.

In the range $j\leq n$, step 2 gives finite-dimensional cohomology groups. A basis of $H^{n-j}(Y,E)$ has the finite dual basis in $\operatorname{Hom}_F(H^{n-j}(Y,E),F)$, so the right-hand space is also finite dimensional. For $j>n$ both sides are zero by step 4. The preceding construction works unchanged for $n=0$; in the empty case every group and every map is zero. None of the invoked pairing or vanishing results requires connectedness or geometric integrality, so all the claimed cases are included.
